improv_read.player_bid: Wren sits, stakes ten gold, says she will play, and watches the dealer's hands.
improv_read.connection: Uktarl profits from seated marks; a paying player is exactly what he wants.
improv_read.kit_choice: Kit lets the dealer make the offer simple and leaves the weight of play to the player.

public_brief.objective: Seat the newcomer in a game he deals and get her stake on the table.
public_brief.tactic: Name the game in a sentence and let her choose how to play it.
public_brief.visible_cue: He squares the deck and smiles at her coins.
public_brief.player_opening: She can choose hands or a single roll for the round.
public_brief.kit_focus: Keep the rules to one plain sentence and hand the choice of cards or one roll straight to her.
public_brief.mirror: steady energy, standard, no humor: crisp and clear about the choice

player_mood.cue: I watch the dealer's hands the whole time

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Your ten gold clinks onto the worn wood. The dealer gathers the deck with a slow sweep, squares it, and smiles at the coins rather than at you.

segments.speaker: Dealer
segments.text: A guest who pays before she speaks, how refreshing. At this table we play Twenty-One Coffins: get close to twenty-one without going over, and you beat me. Ten gold rides on the hand. Now, will you play the cards out, hit by hit, or are you the sort who lets fortune decide the whole round at once?

segments.speaker: Kit
segments.reacts_to: will you play the cards out
